# Conflab surface inventory

Read-only survey of Conflab's launcher ahead of WP-10, taken 2026-08-08 against Conflab as it stands (25 files, 4,610 lines under `bin/`). Nothing in Conflab was written to. This is the evidence the WP-10 config is DERIVED from rather than invented, and it is the "before" half of the equivalence evidence WP-10 owes -- you cannot prove every command still works without first writing down what worked.

Method: every handler read, the helper library read end to end, and each mapping claim checked against devbin's actual catalogue and schema rather than against the design narrative. Where a claim is a finding, it was reproduced by running it.

## The command surface -- 18 commands

`CONFLAB_COMMANDS` (`bin/conflab_helpers:127`) is the single source: `server iex cli daemon app use which build test check fmt db docs version macos release deploy precommit`. Eighteen exactly, which is what WP-10's brief says.

| Command     | Destination                        | Notes                                                                                  |
| ----------- | ---------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `server`    | built-in + config `run:`           | `@builtin` Surfaces row. Conflab also sources `config/.env` and warns when absent      |
| `iex`       | built-in as-is                     | catalogue default `iex -S mix` matches; Conflab adds the same `.env` sourcing          |
| `cli`       | built-in + project handler         | needs `resolve_native_bin`, so the handler stays project-local                         |
| `daemon`    | **project handler**                | passthrough to the binary plus `reload` / `which` / `restart` / `switch`               |
| `app`       | **project handler**                | Conflab.app; `build` / `run` / `reload` / `which` over xcodegen + xcodebuild           |
| `use`       | **project handler**                | dev-vs-brew switcher across CLI, daemon and app                                        |
| `which`     | `opt-in` catalogue row + handler   | row ships with no command line (WP-18); Conflab supplies the recipe                    |
| `build`     | built-in + config `run:`           | `any` row, project declares its own targets                                            |
| `test`      | built-in, 4 options                | `mix` `credo` `rust` `swift` -- all four already in the catalogue                      |
| `check`     | built-in, 6 of 8 options           | see the gate table below -- two gates have no catalogue row                            |
| `fmt`       | built-in, 4 options                | `elixir` `rust` `swift` `md` all present                                               |
| `db`        | built-in, 4 of 7 subs              | Conflab uses `mix ash.*`, catalogue defaults are `mix ecto.*` -- config override       |
| `docs`      | built-in, 2 of 4 subs              | `agents` + `treeindex` ship; `completions` + `publish` are project-local               |
| `version`   | built-in                           | **blocked by issue 0002** -- see Findings                                              |
| `macos`     | `opt-in` catalogue row + handler   | eight subs of signing/notarising; entirely project-local                               |
| `release`   | **project handler**                | tagged release; `release sync` delegates to `version sync`                             |
| `deploy`    | **project handler**                | Fly deploy, server-only                                                                |
| `precommit` | `opt-in` catalogue row + handler   | staged-file subset of `check`                                                          |

**Nine project handlers, not the brief's six.** The six it names are right -- `app` `daemon` `use` `release` `macos` `deploy` -- and `which` and `precommit` are not a seventh and eighth, because they are `opt-in` catalogue rows WP-18 shipped deliberately without command lines, so Conflab declares the recipe and the row supplies the identity.

Three more need handlers the brief does not list, and none of them is a project-specific COMMAND -- each is a built-in whose surrounding behaviour is project-specific:

- `cli` -- needs `resolve_native_bin`, so which of three installed binaries runs is decided project-side.
- `server` and `iex` -- both source `config/.env` before exec. `lib/cmd/server`'s own header already rules this out of the framework by name ("Laksa prints a banner of URLs, Conflab sources config/.env ... none of that belongs to a framework") and gives the two ways out: a config `run:` or a project handler. A `run:` cannot do it -- sourcing a file then exec'ing is a script, and putting one in config is what D1 forbids -- so it is a handler.

That last pair matters more than it looks. Conflab's `server` warns when `config/.env` is absent, precisely because a missing provider key "looks identical to a revoked one three screens later". A migration that drops the sourcing does not fail; it boots on defaults and fails somewhere else.

### The gates

`check` -- eight gates. Six have catalogue rows; two do not, and both absences are already decided.

| Conflab gate | devbin row        | Migrates as                                                               |
| ------------ | ----------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `compile`    | `check.compile`   | as-is                                                                     |
| `format`     | `check.format`    | **needs a config `run:`** -- see finding 3                                |
| `deps`       | `check.deps`      | as-is                                                                     |
| `toolchain`  | `check.toolchain` | as-is (`@builtin`)                                                        |
| `clippy`     | `check.clippy`    | **needs a config `run:`** -- see finding 2                                |
| `critic`     | `check.critic`    | as-is (`@builtin`)                                                        |
| `contract`   | none              | project-specific: shared error-contract literals across Rust and Swift    |
| `parity`     | none              | devbin declines this one deliberately, with its reason in `lib/cmd/check` |

`test` -- four gates, `mix` `credo` `rust` `swift`, all four already in the catalogue with matching command lines and grammars. This is the cleanest part of the migration and it is not a coincidence: `lib/runlog` is a port of Conflab's own sealed-gate subsystem (WP-06).

**The Swift grammar was checked specifically, because it is the one with a history.** Conflab's carries a late repair -- the swift-testing rules were missing and their absence INVERTED the seal, sealing 18 bytes for an assertion failure and 4.5 KB of log tail for a codesign failure. A port taken before that repair would reintroduce it. Devbin's has all four failure shapes, the `recorded an issue` block and the 40-line truncation marker, and it goes further than Conflab's: the three status glyphs are spliced in as bytes rather than written as literals, because `\xNN` is a gawk extension and a silently non-matching rule "would look like success, on the one grammar whose history is precisely that of an inverted seal". Faithful, hardened, and ASCII-clean. No finding.

## The helper library -- 833 lines, and where each part lands

Devbin already absorbed the universal half. Checked function by function against `lib/helpers` and `lib/runlog`.

**Already in devbin, deleted from Conflab on migration:** `die` `warn` `step` `ok` `not_yet` `require_tool` `read_version` `assert_semver` `bump_semver` `strip_ansi` `abs_path` `rlwrap_exec` (`lib/helpers`); `open_run_log` `note_promotion` `write_errors_file` `latest_pointer_keepset` `in_keepset` `purge_run_logs` `refuse_purge_without_log` `purge_only_run_logs` `warn_if_tee_failed` `print_run_verdict` (`lib/runlog`); the four `CONFLAB_*_ERRORS_AWK` grammars and `CONFLAB_AWK_SEG` (`grammar_for` / `grammar_names`); `parse_common_opts` and the `--env` / `--bin` pair (`lib/resolve` + config `options:`); `is_command` / `CONFLAB_COMMANDS` (`lib/resolve` + config); `init_run_colors` (`init_colors`, renamed).

**Stays project-local:** the native-tree layout (`CONFLAB_CRATES` `crate_dir` `crate_manifest` `crate_binary` `macos_project_dir` `macos_app_bundle`), binary resolution (`resolve_native_bin` `describe_native_bin`), the provenance family (`git_head_full` `git_head_stamp` `stamp_matches_head` `bin_stamp` `app_stamp` `report_provenance`), and `sync_cargo_lock`.

That split is exactly what WP-10's brief predicted, naming `crate_dir`, `macos_app_bundle`, `resolve_native_bin` and `report_provenance`. The brief is accurate.

## Findings

### 1. `version` destroys Conflab's two lockfiles, and the gate certifies it -- BLOCKER

Raised as **issue 0002** (`intent/issues/OPEN/0002/`), severity high. Reproduced, not read: `version set` writes the bare version string over any sidecar whose kind devbin has no recipe for, and Conflab declares `native/cli/Cargo.lock` and `native/daemon/Cargo.lock`. `check` then reports drift, tells the user to run `sync`, `sync` destroys the file, and the next `check` reports "every sidecar agrees". Green gate, destroyed file.

The default branch is **not** an oversight, and the issue does not ask for it to be removed: `docs/configuration.md:41` documents it and `tests/unit/version.bats:144` tests it with a `plain.txt` sidecar that really is a bare version file. The defect is that devbin dispatches on filename and then writes content it never inspected, so it cannot tell that case from a structured file -- and resolves the ambiguity destructively while reporting success. That distinction matters for the fix: refusing every unrecognised sidecar would break the documented case.

This blocks WP-10 at its second deliverable. `release sync` also delegates to `version sync`, so the destructive path has two entrances.

### 2. The clippy default is stricter than Conflab's CI, against a stated ruling

Catalogue: `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings`. Conflab: `cargo clippy --manifest-path ... -- -D warnings`, with the reason inline at `bin/conflab_check`:

> clippy runs without `--all-targets` because CI does. A local gate stricter than CI blocks commits CI would have accepted, which teaches people to reach for `--no-verify`.

Not a framework defect -- config overrides it in one line. It is a migration trap, and it is the board's watch-out about prose carrying rulings, arriving early: the ruling is in a comment, not in a spec, and a migration that rewrites the prose without extracting it first loses it silently. The failure is invisible, because a stricter gate still passes on a clean tree; it bites the first time someone is blocked by a lint CI would have allowed.

### 3. `check format` would silently check less than it does today

Conflab's `check_format` runs `mix format --check-formatted` AND `cargo fmt --check` over both crates. Devbin's `check.format` row is `elixir`-scoped and elixir-only. Devbin ships `fmt.rust` (mutating) but no rust counterpart on the non-mutating side, so a straight migration leaves Rust formatting unchecked while the gate still exits 0.

A coverage regression that no exit-code comparison detects: both gates go green on a clean tree. It is caught only by comparing what each gate EXAMINES, which is why the WP-10 acceptance criteria ask for that explicitly rather than for a before/after exit code.

### 4. `db` defaults are Ecto, Conflab is Ash

Catalogue rows are `mix ecto.setup` / `ecto.migrate` / `ecto.reset`; Conflab runs `mix ash.setup` / `ash.migrate` / `ash.reset`. A config override per option, no framework change. Recorded so it is not rediscovered mid-migration.

`db codegen`, `db proxy` and `db sql` have no rows: the first two are declined by devbin with reasons recorded in `lib/cmd/db`, and `sql` is Conflab-specific (it folds `bin/flysql`).

### 5. Conflab's `check` header synopsis omits `contract`

`bin/conflab_check`'s header comment opens `conflab check <compile|format|deps|toolchain|clippy|critic|parity|all>` -- seven gates where the dispatch has eight. Checked before writing it down: the RUNTIME error string names all eight, and `check_all` runs all eight, so nothing is unreachable and no gate is skipped. It is a stale comment and nothing more.

It is recorded because that header comment is the natural source for the `check` help topic, and the help extraction (WP-10's share of the 70 topics) will read it. A synopsis that has drifted from the dispatch is exactly the sort of thing that gets faithfully carried across into authored help and then outlives the file it came from.

## Coverage -- what was checked, and what was not

Stated so the gaps are visible rather than assumed away.

**Read end to end:** `conflab` (the dispatcher), `conflab_helpers` (833 lines, mapped function by function), `conflab_server`, `conflab_iex`, `conflab_cli`, `conflab_docs`, `conflab_fmt`. **Read structurally** -- header, dispatch table and the specific functions a mapping claim rests on: `conflab_check` (`check_format` and `check_clippy` in full), `conflab_test`, `conflab_db`, `conflab_version`, `conflab_daemon`, `conflab_app`, `conflab_use`, `conflab_which`, `conflab_precommit`, `conflab_deploy`, `conflab_macos`, `conflab_release`.

**Checked by running, against devbin rather than Conflab:** the version-sidecar path, twice, before and after the fix; the `check` and `fmt` option surfaces in a mixed elixir/rust/swift fixture. Nothing was executed inside Conflab -- not even a read-only gate, because several of its gates shell out to formatters and builders.

**Verified on disk:** all six declared version sidecars exist at their stated paths, so the failure WP-10 meets there is issue 0002's kind and not a stale path.

**Not read, and the risk that carries:**

- The four sealed runners (`conflab_test_{mix,credo,rust,swift}`, 751 lines). Their GRAMMARS were compared against devbin's and the Swift one checked closely; their runner bodies were not. WP-06 ported this subsystem whole, so the residual risk is in Conflab-specific flags, not in the mechanism.
- `conflab_help`'s 568 lines. Deliberate: `help-migration.md` already rules on all 70 topics, and re-deriving that here would be a second source for it.
- The bodies of `conflab_use` (349), `conflab_release` (334) and `conflab_macos`. All three become project handlers carried across largely intact, so their internals do not bear on the config or the seam. They will need reading when they are moved.
- `conflab_check`'s six other gate bodies. `format` and `clippy` were read because the mapping claims rest on them; the rest map to catalogue rows by name and command line.

**Not retired by any of this:** the elixir, rust and swift gate families still have never run against a real toolchain. That is AC-10.12, and it cannot be discharged from here.

## What this changes about WP-10's deliverables

The brief was written 2026-08-05, before WP-14 to WP-18 shipped the built-in library, before WP-12's docs and before WP-13's ten fixes. Read against what has landed since, it holds up better than the five WPs that preceded it -- the 18 commands, the eight and four gates, the six sidecars, the six project handlers and the named project-local helpers are all accurate.

Three corrections, each carried as an AC rather than absorbed quietly:

1. **`which` and `precommit` need naming.** The brief's "six Conflab-specific commands" is right, but it leaves these two unaccounted for. They are `opt-in` catalogue rows from WP-18 needing a project-supplied recipe -- a third category the brief predates.
2. **Three more commands need project handlers**, none of which the brief lists: `cli` (binary resolution), and `server` and `iex` (both source `config/.env`, which the framework rules out by name and a `run:` cannot express). Nine handlers, not six -- the single largest correction here, and the one that most changes the size of the job.
3. **The equivalence evidence must compare gate COVERAGE, not just exit codes.** The brief asks for "every command and subcommand that worked before works after", captured as a before/after transcript, with sealed gates compared on their seal files. Finding 3 is invisible to all of that: both gates go green, and both seals are empty. What discriminates is what each gate examined.
